title: High-Resolution Downscaled CMIP6 Projections dataset of Key Climate Variables for Senegal
abstract: A high-resolution climate projections dataset is produced by statistically downscaling climate projections from the CMIP6 experiment. This global dataset is at a spatial resolution of 0.0375° × 0.0375° from 19 climate models over Senegal domain. It includes five essential surface daily variables: mean, minimum, and maximum air temperatures, precipitation, and terrestrial radiation. The dataset covers daily climate data for the historical period (1850-2014) and future projections (2015-2100) for three greenhouse gas emissions scenarios: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5. The downscaling method used is the "Cumulative Distribution Function-transform", which is utilized for bias correction and has been widely referenced in peer-reviewed literature. The data processing includes rigorous quality control of metadata following climate modelling community standards and outlier detection to ensure data integrity.
problem: Global climate models from the CMIP6 project exhibit significant biases and coarse resolution, particularly in tropical regions like the Sahel, which can lead to considerable errors in local impact assessments for sensitive applications such as agricultural planning.
method: This paper proposes a statistical downscaling method using the Cumulative Distribution Function-transform (CDF-t) to produce a high-resolution, bias-corrected dataset of key climate variables for Senegal from 19 CMIP6 models.
task: The task is to produce a high-resolution dataset of key climate variables for Senegal by statistically downscaling climate projections from the CMIP6 experiment, covering historical and future periods under different emissions scenarios.
innovation: This paper presents a high-resolution, bias-corrected, and downscaled dataset of key daily climate variables for Senegal, derived from 19 CMIP6 models to provide projections for historical (1850–2014) and future (2015–2100) periods under three emission scenarios.

The raw simulations of the NorESM Climate Modelling Consortium (NCC) show the best performance in reproducing the climatology, with an average bias of less than 10 mm for NorLM (Supplemental material Table S4).

At the regional scale, the uncorrected models show a bias for the mean maximum temperatures ranging from -3.67 °C (CNRMCM6) to +5.59 °C (MIROC6). In contrast, the ensemble average of the biases of the corrected models is much smaller, only 0.15 °C (Supplemental material Table S4).
